subject: general
question: Between the ninth and eleventh centuries, the_________ style was used for the sculptures in Bengal (including Bangladesh) and Bihar.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Pala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When Bengali and Odia cultures united during Chaitanya's journey to Orissa in 1510 CE, Pala Gaan might have come to light.
 
• This art is performed by a group of five or six people.
 
• Gayaka, the main singer, Bayaka, the drummer, and Palia make up the group (Chorus).
 
• The Gayaka wields a "Chamara" (fly whisker) with great flair and holds a pair of cymbals in his right hand.
 
• He recounts puranic text stories interspersed with justifications.
 
• Along with Gayaka, the choir dances in very short, repetitive movements.
 
• The Mahabharata by Sarala Das mentions Pala.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Pala did on the occasion of "Satyanarayana puja" or "Ekousia," which is observed on the 21st day after a child's birth.
 
• The worship of Lord Satyanarayana is connected to both two types of Pala.
 
• They are Thia (standing) and Baithaki (sitting) (standing).
 
• Sometimes, particularly on the occasion of ceremonial celebrations, competitions between two or more groups are sometimes set up, in which each group makes an effort to demonstrate its best qualities.
